channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: South Korean Won: Undervaluation and BOK outlook aid won – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights an extended broad rally in South Korean Won (KRW) as Korean equities underperform, reducing rebalancing outflows.

item.title: Japenese Yen falls as Fed minutes revive tightening bets
item.description: The Japanese Yen depreciated by over 0.26% within familiar levels, as the Fed’s last meeting minutes showed that the majority of participants indicated that “some policy firming would likely be warranted” and agreed to shorten the length of the monetary policy statement.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Bears retain control within descending channel
item.description: EUR/USD holds firm on Wednesday after reversing earlier losses triggered by renewed tensions between the United States (US) and Iran, while traders digest the June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting minutes.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Short-term losses versus upside risks against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD is edging higher after a period of tight consolidation, with intraday upside seen as limited below nearby resistance.

item.title: US Dollar Index shrugs at unanimous Fed hold that reads anything but unanimous
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) spent Wednesday travelling in circles, grinding around 101.00 after the Minutes of the June 16-17 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting crossed the wires at 18:00 GMT, capping a session in which traders had already faded another round of Middle East friction.

item.title: Breaking: FOMC Minutes lean toward higher-for-longer narrative
item.description: The June FOMC Minutes reinforced the Fed’s cautious approach as policymakers unanimously agreed to maintain interest rates unchanged while keeping a close eye on inflation risks.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ tightening supports upside – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO’s Georgette Boele reports that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand lifted its policy rate by 25 bp to 2.5% and signalled more tightening is likely. Despite some easing in energy prices, the bank sees persistent inflation pressures and scope for further reduction in stimulus.

item.title: Gold slips as Trump’s Iran warning lifts US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price dives over 1.30% on Wednesday as tensions in the Middle East bolstered the Greenback after US President Donald Trump said that the agreement to end the war with Iran was “over.” At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades at $4,059 after hitting a four-day low of $4,021.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG extends lower low sequence, eyes on $55
item.description: Silver prices collapse nearly 2.50% on Wednesday as risk aversion drives traders towards buying the US Dollar, to the detriment of precious metals. At the time of writing, the XAG/USD trades at $58.41 after waking at around $61.03.

item.title: WTI rises as supply disruption fears return to Oil markets
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trims part of its earlier gains on Wednesday but remains supported as supply risks resurface amid escalating tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: British Pound feeds on bad news as the Euro slides to a one-year low
item.description: The Euro's slide against the Pound has now consumed seven of the last eight trading sessions, and the reflex explanation of a soft single currency gets the attribution backwards.

item.title: Japanese Yen falls near multi-decade lows
item.description: USD/JPY trades higher near 162.50 on Wednesday, after nearing a four-decade high earlier in the day, as the US Dollar (USD) remains supported by geopolitical risk and caution ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) Minutes.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed repricing after hawkish pivot – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report that the US Dollar (USD) is trading mixed as renewed Iran tensions hit risk appetite, with stocks falling and Oil (Brent) jumping 6%.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average learns the old war playbook now runs in reverse
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average opened Wednesday within a few points of its 52,847 session high and spent the rest of the day paying down three weeks of ceasefire faith, giving back 700 points through the day.

item.title: Asia FX: Diverging paths under Dollar strength – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan highlights that external pressures on Asia FX persist as the US Dollar and US Treasury yields stay firm, with markets fully pricing another Fed hike by October.

item.title: Gold slides as US-Iran tensions revive Fed rate hike bets, FOMC Minutes loom
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) sees a sharp move lower on Wednesday after US President Donald Trump declared that the ceasefire deal with Iran was “over” during the NATO Summit in Ankara, Turkey. However, Reuters later reported that Trump did not repeat those remarks, citing a source familiar with the talks.

item.title: Canadian Dollar strengthens on Oil rally as markets eye jobs data
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.4190 at the time of writing on Wednesday, down 0.10% on the day, as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) benefits from a sharp rebound in Oil prices fueled by renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Euro: Energy repricing shapes outlook against US Dollar – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO’s Georgette Boele notes that the Euro’s relationship with energy prices has evolved, with recent Oil and Gas gains again weighing on EUR/USD.

item.title: British Pound holds firm as Hormuz shock lifts Oil, Dollar
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) posts modest gains during the North American session on Wednesday amid growing tensions in the Middle East, as US President Donald Trump's said the deal with Iran was “over” after both countries exchanged attacks over the last couple of days.

item.title: United States Dollar Index climbs as Middle East tensions, Fed rate hike bets lift demand
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) consolidates modest gains on Wednesday as traders assess renewed tensions between the United States and Iran and the potential economic fallout.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Oil shock weighs JPY against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight renewed weakness in the Japanese Yen (JPY), which is underperforming G10 peers and threatening fresh multi-decade lows as USD/JPY trades at levels last seen in 1986.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ hike underpins kiwi – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole reports that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) raised rates to 2.50%, delivering a more hawkish message than expected and signalling further tightening is likely.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains pressured amid Trump comments
item.description: AUD/USD trades under pressure near 0.6920 on Wednesday, following the US Dollar (USD) holding firm amid geopolitical risk and caution ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) Minutes.

item.title: United Kingdom: Market watching Burnham – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses UK political dynamics, noting Burnham’s likely unchallenged path to becoming Prime Minister on July 20 and his popularity within Labour.

item.title: British Pound: Recovery eyes 1.36 against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the British Pound (GBP) is slightly softer but supported by a sharp repricing of Bank of England (BoE) tightening.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Hawkish Fed minutes may support greenback – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that recent equity jitters and firm Oil prices have underlined the Dollar’s safe-haven appeal, while markets look to the June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes.

item.title: India: Gradual firming CPI supports RBI patience – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategist Kunal Kundu expects India’s June 2026 headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation to print around 4.1% year-on-year, slightly above May’s 3.9% but still within the RBI’s tolerance band.

item.title: Silver falls as Trump renews Iran threats, boosts US Dollar ahead of Fed Minutes
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its decline on Wednesday and trades around $58.45 at the time of writing. The white metal remains under pressure after comments from US President Donald Trump revived concerns about renewed conflict in the Middle East, supporting the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields.

item.title: Euro steadies above 1.1400 as traders assess US-Iran tensions
item.description: EUR/USD treads water above the 1.1400 mark on Wednesday, steadying after coming under selling pressure as traders assess renewed US-Iran tensions after both sides exchanged fire overnight following attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz earlier this week.

item.title: Mexican Peso: High real yields underpin MXN demand – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Christian Lawrence and Molly Schwartz note that despite Moody’s downgrade of Mexico to Baa3, 10-year MBono yields have fallen and markets remain relaxed about Mexico’s investment-grade status.
